title: Why Is China Less Active in the 2026 Ebola Epidemic?
author: Zhida Shang
text:
An Ebola treatment center in Bunia, the DRC, constructed by the World Health Organization.
Credit: © WHO / Grainne Harrington
The Ebola epidemic spreading through the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) could become the largest Ebola outbreak on record if infections continue at their current pace. More than 6,700 people had been infected and more than 3,200 had died by September 2026. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo virus, a form of Ebola for which there is currently no licensed vaccine or approved treatment.The crisis is unfolding at a remarkable moment for global health. The United States is retreating from the global health system it once led. Beijing is the world’s second-largest economy and holds substantial interests in the DRC’s copper and cobalt industries. That matters not because Beijing has an obligation to replace Washington. Rather, the outbreak offers a test of whether, as the United States pulls back from global institutions, China will step forward.[...]
